findings.title: Legacy SQL-command path bypasses the new SQL-expression gate
findings.body: UnmarshalSQLCommand creates a SQLCommand via NewSQLCommand without checking enableSqlExpressions or the sqlExpressions feature toggle, unlike the new check in ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery. This legacy unmarshalling path therefore is not explicitly disabled; it currently fails only incidentally because sql.TablesList now delegates to the stub DB and errors. If the DuckDB-backed DB implementation is restored or replaced, this path would re-enable SQL expressions (the CVE-2024-9264 surface) without passing the gate. Gate or reject SQL in UnmarshalSQLCommand/NewSQLCommand as defense-in-depth.

findings.title: Disabled-SQL check can panic on a nil FeatureToggles
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions unconditionally calls h.features.IsEnabledGlobally even though it always returns false. If an ExpressionQueryReader is constructed without feature toggles (nil interface, e.g. in tests or other direct constructions), a SQL-type query now panics with a nil dereference instead of returning the intended 'not implemented' error. Since the result is unconditionally disabled, return false without dereferencing h.features.

findings.title: enableSqlExpressions has inverted, dead logic
findings.body: The helper computes enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions), then returns false both when that value is true and in the fallthrough, so the flag and the branch are dead and the naming is inverted. This is misleading for a security-sensitive gate: a future editor following the variable name could easily re-enable the vulnerable path by 'fixing' the apparent inversion. Replace it with an explicit unconditional return false (with a comment referencing the removal), or remove the helper.

findings.title: Stub DB breaks existing SQL tests with no updated/disabled tests
findings.body: NewInMemoryDB's RunCommands and QueryFramesInto now always return 'not implemented', so the package-level TablesList in pkg/expr/sql/parser.go always errors and NewSQLCommand always rejects queries. The PR adds no test verifying SQL expressions are rejected, and does not update or skip the existing parser/SQL-command tests that expect DuckDB-backed table extraction and execution to succeed, leaving them failing against this stub. Update/skip those tests and add a regression test that a SQL expression is rejected regardless of the feature toggle.
